answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and incumbent's refusal to renegotiate force action. memory_c2 provides direct precedent: switching to the low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and reliable invoicing. This vendor can likely close the 18% gap. The assembly line's 94% utilization creates delivery risk—verification of memory_c2's success reduces that risk to acceptable levels. However, this action locks capacity to one vendor without a safety net (unlike memory_c3's dual-sourcing approach). The 14-day window prevents parallel negotiation or incremental testing. Deferring (memory_c5) would lose budget flexibility mid-year. Renewing (memory_c1) fails the mandate. A standard_experiment scope on the new vendor with early quality gates mitigates execution risk while committing to the cost target.
